title: Weight fetch heuristics — scratchpad (model-loading breadcrumbs)
content:
Context:
- Model: open-llm-xlarge-v2 (converted from hf checkpoint).
- Deployment: dedicated; staging pool (gpu-a100-40gb); failing on ~5% of cold-starts.
- Symptom: process aborts during weights unpack / shard map apply. Instances that fail often succeed on retry.

Observed behavior (notes):
- Failure window: 2025-02-25 — 2025-03-07, intermittent across multiple hosts.
- Pattern: first attempt after instance boot sometimes fails; subsequent curl/gsutil retries succeed.
- Error excerpts (collected):
  * Python trace (loader):
    Traceback (most recent call last):
      File "/opt/runtime/loader.py", line 312, in load_weights
        shard = torch.load(f, map_location='cpu')
    EOFError: Ran out of input

  * Another run: partial tar read error from tarfile module:
    tarfile.ReadError: file could not be opened as archive

  * Loader validation stage: sha256 mismatch for shard_07: expected 3f1a... got 0000...

Commands and ad-hoc checks tried:
- Manual download to reproduce:
  TIME: 2025-03-02T09:14Z
  $ gsutil -m cp gs://model-buckets/open-llm-xlarge-v2/shards/* /tmp/shards/
  (observed one object re-download with zero-size temp file in /tmp/shards/.filepart)

- Verified blob checksums:
  $ gsutil hash -h gs://model-buckets/open-llm-xlarge-v2/shards/shard_07.pt
  Hash (crc32c): ...
  Etag (md5): ...
  -> matched upstream expected at rest

- Local sha verify after cp:
  $ sha256sum /tmp/shards/shard_07.pt
  3f1a...  /tmp/shards/shard_07.pt  (OK on successful runs)

- Replicated network flakiness: used curl with --retry and --max-time to force timeout and see behavior:
  $ curl -f --retry 5 --retry-delay 2 -o /tmp/shards/shard_07.pt https://storage.example/shard_07.pt
  -> On simulated 2xx then reset returned partial file (smaller size); loader saw EOFError.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Partial object write to FS during streaming -> loader opens file before write complete. race with atomic move missing.
   - Evidence: presence of .part or .tmp files on some hosts, 0-byte temporary artifacts.
2) Shard manifest (shard_map.json) occasionally points to older artifact or transiently-incomplete replica.
   - Evidence: occasionally md5/sha mismatch logs; but bucket-level hashes usually OK.
3) Underlying object store returning truncated responses when client cancels / network resets (e.g., HTTP 200 with truncated body).
4) Local container overlayfs/disk pressure causing write failures that are swallowed by downloader and leave partial files.

Immediate mitigation attempts (notes):
- Introduced atomic download pattern: write to /tmp/<name>.partial then mv to final after size and checksum verified.
  - Local test: reduced EOFError occurrences to 0 in 50 trial starts.
- Increased downloader retries and added Content-Length validation post-download (compare to HEAD).
- Added explicit fsync after file write in downloader to avoid delayed write visibility.

Reproducer steps (minimal):
1) Boot a fresh staging instance (gpu-a100-40gb).
2) Start runtime with env flags: RUNTIME_SHARD_DOWNLOAD_PARALLEL=8 RUNTIME_DOWNLOAD_RETRY=3 RUNTIME_LOG_LEVEL=debug
3) Simulate truncated transfer (on storage proxy): e.g., drop packets after N bytes using tc/netem or a small python http server that returns partial body.
4) Observe loader behaviour: sometimes torch.load raises EOFError.

Key log snippets (sanitized):
- 2025-03-01T18:07:11Z [loader] INFO starting shard fetch: shard_07.pt -> /tmp/shards/shard_07.pt
- 2025-03-01T18:07:12Z [downloader] WARN size mismatch: got 0 bytes; retrying
- 2025-03-01T18:07:12Z [loader] ERROR EOFError while loading /tmp/shards/shard_07.pt
- 2025-03-01T18:07:12Z [sentry] capture: RuntimeError("unexpected EOF while reading file")

Notes about shard map / manifest format (for context):
- shard_map.json: list of {"shard_id":7, "path":"gs://.../shard_07.pt", "sha256":"3f1a...", "size":16777216}
- Our loader currently trusts size reported by downloader, but does not compare to manifest size until after torch.load call (bad ordering).

What I changed locally (sketch):
- downloader.py: after write, run verify_size_and_hash(file, expected_size, expected_sha)
  - if mismatch -> delete and retry
  - atomic mv only after verify
- loader.py: defer torch.load until verification step passes for all shards.

Open questions / TODOs:
- (A) Why do some hosts show .filepart/0-byte artifacts even with gsutil -m cp? investigate container storage driver (overlayfs) + ephemeral disk provisioning code path.
- (B) Are there intermediate proxies that prematurely close connections? ask infra to check storage-proxy logs around failure windows.
- (C) Should we add a preflight HEAD request and rely on Content-Length + ETag before streaming? tradeoff: doubles requests for many shards.
- (D) Add metric: downloads_verified_success / downloads_failed_checksum -> expose in console for model loads.

Next steps (short):
- Push downloader change (atomic write + verify) to a feature branch. (PR drafted: runtime/pr/421)
- Add metric + alert on repeated checksum failures (JIRA-MLINF-88).
- Infra: request CDN/storage team to surface truncated-transfer counts for the bucket and proxy.
- Run 100 cold-starts in lab with fault injection to validate decrease in EOF/ReadError.

Random notes / heuristics that helped during triage:
- Do not call torch.load on the file before verifying its length and sha. torch.load happily throws obscure EOFError which hides root cause.
- Check for userland decompression: some objects are gunzipped on the fly by proxies -> size in manifest may be post-decompression. We should standardize on stored compression metadata.
- When reproducing, simpler to use an nginx local server with slice of file served to simulate truncation.

Last adhoc commands (for reference):
- check inode + overlayfs layering:
  $ df -h /tmp/shards; sudo findmnt -o SOURCE,TARGET /tmp/shards
  $ sudo debugfs -R "stat <inode>" /dev/nvme0n1p1

- quick python reproducer for truncated server (used in lab):
  import socket
  s=socket.socket(); s.bind(("0.0.0.0",8080)); s.listen(1)
  conn, _ = s.accept()
  data = conn.recv(1024)
  conn.sendall(b"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 100000\r\n\r\n" + b"A"*4096)
  conn.close()
  # client saves 4KB file (truncated) -> loader EOF on torch.load

If anyone hits this: ping me (Devin) in #eng-serving-runtime. I'll attach the small failing shard (sanitized) and the runner script.

Revision history:
- 2025-02-13 created initial scratchpad
- 2025-03-02 added reproducer steps and early mitigation notes
- 2025-03-09 added final local-test results (atomic mv + verify reduced failures in lab)
